es.description: Ponferrada mantiene una vigilancia constante en Manzanedo de Valdueza ante el riesgo de desprendimientos por las precipitaciones. De forma paralela, el consistorio decreta el cierre de los parques públicos debido a rachas de viento que superan los cuarenta kilómetros por hora. es.description: Comprar un coche nuevo en España garantiza, como mínimo, tres años de cobertura desde enero de 2022, aunque ese suelo legal es solo el punto de partida. pl.title: Maciej Maciusiak dla WP SportoweFakty: Hejt? Biorę na klatę. Gorzej nasze dzieci
pl.description: - Jestem trenerem głównym i przyjmuję pewne rzeczy na klatę. Oczywiście czasem jest bardzo przykro czytać krytykę, ale rozumiem, że kibic śledzący skoki przed telewizorem chce, żeby reprezentacja Polski odnosiła sukcesy. Ja gdy oglądam piłkę nożną czy inne sporty, też trzymam za Polaków kciuki, a jak nie idzie, to się denerwuję. W skokach te nerwy w większości spadały na mnie, ale też nauczyłem się z tym żyć - mówi WP SportoweFakty Maciej Maciusiak u progu nowego sezonu w skokach narciarskich. Poprzedni sezon, pierwszy w roli trenera głównego, był dla Maciusiaka momentami piękny, przede wszystkim na igrzyskach Mediolan-Cortina 2026, w których skoczkowie zdobyli trzy medale. Ale bywało też bardzo trudno, gdy brakowało wyników w Pucharze Świata. - Po mnie raczej to spływa, ale rodziny bardziej z tym zostają, bo są w kraju, czytają to wszystko. Czasem są takie sytuacje, że siedzimy na kolacji po zawodach i dostaję telefon z Polski: co się tam u was dzieje? A my o niczym nie wiemy, bo u nas się nic nie dzieje, to jakieś niesprawdzone informacje. Moja żona się już nauczyła z tego żartować, ale są dzieciaki, jest dalsza rodzina. No ale w takim świecie żyjemy i za wszelką cenę też nie będziemy z tym walczyć. A ja czasem jak jakiś tekst czytam to też zajrzę do komentarzy. No jak jest coś śmiesznego, to dlaczego nie? - mówi Maciusiak. To on był jednym z tych, którzy zabiegali o powrót do Polski Stefana Horngachera w roli koordynatora szkolenia. Zachwala współpracę z nim i śmieje się, że na razie żaden ze starszych zawodników kadry nie ogłosił, że chce pójść w ślady Kamila Stocha i zakończyć karierę. - Z każdym z tych zawodników na na koniec sezonu przeprowadzałem rozmowy, pytając jakie mają mają plany. I wtedy wszyscy, którzy którzy są w kadrze - Maciej Kot, Dawid Kubacki, Piotr Żyła - zgłaszali pełną gotowość do treningów. U nas w każdej grupie młodość z rutyną się przeplata, to jest bardzo fajne, bo oni mogą się czegoś nawzajem uczyć. Kacper Tomasiak zrobił kolejny kolejny postęp, szczególnie w technice i w motoryce. A poza skocznią jest dokładnie taki jak był, popularność go nie zmieniła i życzę mu tego, żeby pozostał zawsze taki jak jest. Klimek Joniak to też wielki talent, pokazał to w Klingenthal, gdzie konkurs był bardzo mocno obsadzony, można powiedzieć cała czołówka światowa skakała w tych zawodach - mówi Maciusiak o miejscu Joniaka na podium w ostatnim konkursie Letniej Grand Prix. Sezon Pucharu Świata zaczyna się w piątek w Lillehammer konkursem mikstów, a w sobotę i niedzielę zostaną rozegrane po dwa konkursy - kobiet i mężczyzn.

gr.title: Μαρουσάκης: Αλλάζει ο καιρός από τη Δευτέρα -Δεν φεύγει η ζέστη, αλλά έρχονται βροχές και καταιγίδες
gr.description: Με εναλλαγές συννεφιάς και ηλιοφάνειας θα κυλήσει η Παρασκευή στις περισσότερες περιοχές της χώρας, όμως από Κυριακή και κυρίως Δευτέρα αναμένεται νέα μεταβολή του καιρού, με βροχές και καταιγίδες. Σύμφωνα με την πρόγνωση του Κλέαρχου Μαρουσάκη, για σήμερα αναμένονται διαστήματα ηλιοφάνειας, ενώ στη δυτική Ελλάδα θα αναπτυχθούν νεφώσεις που θα συνοδεύονται από τοπικές βροχές. Ασθενή φαινόμενα ενδέχεται να σημειωθούν επίσης στο βόρειο Αιγαίο και στα βορειοανατολικά ηπειρωτικά. Οι άνεμοι θα πνέουν από νότιες και νοτιοδυτικές διευθύνσεις, κατά τόπους με ισχυρές εντάσεις. Από το απόγευμα θα στραφούν σε βορειοδυτικούς, μεταφέροντας ψυχρότερες αέριες μάζες, που θα γίνουν περισσότερο αισθητές το σαββατοκύριακο. Όμως, οι νοτιάδες τις τελευταίες ώρες ευνοούν τη μεταφορά θερμότερων αερίων μαζών και διατηρούν τη θερμοκρασία σε υψηλά για την εποχή επίπεδα. Η ημέρα θα ξεκινήσει με ήπιες θερμοκρασίες, που θα θυμίζουν άνοιξη. Το μεσημέρι ο υδράργυρος θα φτάσει στους 26 με 28 βαθμούς Κελσίου στα βορειοανατολικά ηπειρωτικά και στη βόρεια Κρήτη, ενώ τοπικά ενδέχεται να κινηθεί ακόμη υψηλότερα. Στα δυτικά και βόρεια η θερμοκρασία θα είναι λίγο χαμηλότερη, εξαιτίας των νεφώσεων και των τοπικών βροχών. Στην Αττική, η ημέρα θα ξεκινήσει με καλές καιρικές συνθήκες και μεγάλα διαστήματα ηλιοφάνειας έως αργά το μεσημέρι. Από τις πρώτες βραδινές ώρες αναμένεται να περάσουν πιο οργανωμένες νεφώσεις, χωρίς να προκαλέσουν αξιόλογα φαινόμενα. Οι άνεμοι στα πελάγη θα φτάσουν τα 6 - 7 μποφόρ, ενώ η θερμοκρασία θα αγγίξει τους 26 βαθμούς, με τις υψηλότερες τιμές να καταγράφονται στα ανατολικά του νομού. Στη Θεσσαλονίκη υπάρχει πιθανότητα σχηματισμού ομίχλης, ενώ θα εναλλάσσονται τα διαστήματα συννεφιάς με την ηλιοφάνεια. Σταδιακά θα επικρατήσει βαρδάρης και η θερμοκρασία θα κυμανθεί από 23 έως 24 βαθμούς Κελσίου. Πότε έρχονται οι βροχές και οι καταιγίδες Σύμφωνα με τον Κλέαρχο Μαρουσάκη, το Σάββατο και η Κυριακή θα είναι καλές μέρες, με πιο καθαρή ατμόσφαιρα, βορειοδυτικούς ανέμους και μείωση της υγρασίας. Η θερμοκρασία θα υποχωρήσει, ενώ τις νυχτερινές και πρώτες πρωινές ώρες θα κάνει αρκετό κρύο, κυρίως στα κεντρικά και βόρεια ηπειρωτικά. Το βράδυ του Σαββάτου προς την Κυριακή, και από την Κυριακή προς τη Δευτέρα, δεν αποκλείεται να καταγραφούν ακόμη και μονοψήφιες θερμοκρασίες στον ηπειρωτικό κορμό της χώρας, σύμφωνα με τον μετεωρολόγο του Open. Ωστόσο, την Κυριακή και κυρίως τη Δευτέρα αναμένεται να προσεγγίσει τη χώρα νέα κακοκαιρία από τα βόρεια Βαλκάνια. Το σύστημα θα διαμορφώσει και πάλι τον καιρό τύπου «Π», με βροχές και καταιγίδες κατά την έναρξη της νέας εβδομάδας, κυρίως στα δυτικά και βορειοδυτικά τμήματα. Η νέα εβδομάδα θα ξεκινήσει με βροχερό σκηνικό και νοτιάδες, οι οποίοι αναμένεται να κυριαρχήσουν καθ' όλη τη διάρκειά της. Η θερμοκρασία θα παρουσιάσει και πάλι άνοδο, ενώ θα αυξηθούν τα επίπεδα υγρασίας. Τα περισσότερα φαινόμενα αναμένονται να εντοπίζονται στις περιμετρικές περιοχές της χώρας, ενώ ανοιχτό παραμένει το ενδεχόμενο μεταφοράς αφρικανικής σκόνης. Όμως, οι νοτιάδες τις τελευταίες ώρες ευνοούν τη μεταφορά θερμότερων αερίων μαζών και διατηρούν τη θερμοκρασία σε υψηλά για την εποχή επίπεδα. Η ημέρα θα ξεκινήσει με ήπιες θερμοκρασίες, που θα θυμίζουν άνοιξη. Το μεσημέρι ο υδράργυρος θα φτάσει στους 26 με 28 βαθμούς Κελσίου στα βορειοανατολικά ηπειρωτικά και στη βόρεια Κρήτη, ενώ τοπικά ενδέχεται να κινηθεί ακόμη υψηλότερα. Στην Αττική, η ημέρα θα ξεκινήσει με καλές καιρικές συνθήκες και μεγάλα διαστήματα ηλιοφάνειας έως αργά το μεσημέρι. Από τις πρώτες βραδινές ώρες αναμένεται να περάσουν πιο οργανωμένες νεφώσεις, χωρίς να προκαλέσουν αξιόλογα φαινόμενα. Οι άνεμοι στα πελάγη θα φτάσουν τα 6 - 7 μποφόρ, ενώ η θερμοκρασία θα αγγίξει τους 26 βαθμούς, με τις υψηλότερες τιμές να καταγράφονται στα ανατολικά του νομού. Στη Θεσσαλονίκη υπάρχει πιθανότητα σχηματισμού ομίχλης, ενώ θα εναλλάσσονται τα διαστήματα συννεφιάς με την ηλιοφάνεια. Σταδιακά θα επικρατήσει βαρδάρης και η θερμοκρασία θα κυμανθεί από 23 έως 24 βαθμούς Κελσίου. Σύμφωνα με τον Κλέαρχο Μαρουσάκη, το Σάββατο και η Κυριακή θα είναι καλές μέρες, με πιο καθαρή ατμόσφαιρα, βορειοδυτικούς ανέμους και μείωση της υγρασίας. Η θερμοκρασία θα υποχωρήσει, ενώ τις νυχτερινές και πρώτες πρωινές ώρες θα κάνει αρκετό κρύο, κυρίως στα κεντρικά και βόρεια ηπειρωτικά. Το βράδυ του Σαββάτου προς την Κυριακή, και από την Κυριακή προς τη Δευτέρα, δεν αποκλείεται να καταγραφούν ακόμη και μονοψήφιες θερμοκρασίες στον ηπειρωτικό κορμό της χώρας, σύμφωνα με τον μετεωρολόγο του Open. Ωστόσο, την Κυριακή και κυρίως τη Δευτέρα αναμένεται να προσεγγίσει τη χώρα νέα κακοκαιρία από τα βόρεια Βαλκάνια. Το σύστημα θα διαμορφώσει και πάλι τον καιρό τύπου «Π», με βροχές και καταιγίδες κατά την έναρξη της νέας εβδομάδας, κυρίως στα δυτικά και βορειοδυτικά τμήματα. Η νέα εβδομάδα θα ξεκινήσει με βροχερό σκηνικό και νοτιάδες, οι οποίοι αναμένεται να κυριαρχήσουν καθ' όλη τη διάρκειά της. Η θερμοκρασία θα παρουσιάσει και πάλι άνοδο, ενώ θα αυξηθούν τα επίπεδα υγρασίας. Τα περισσότερα φαινόμενα αναμένονται να εντοπίζονται στις περιμετρικές περιοχές της χώρας, ενώ ανοιχτό παραμένει το ενδεχόμενο μεταφοράς αφρικανικής σκόνης. Σύμφωνα με τον ίδιο, ο Δεκέμβριος ενδέχεται να κινηθεί σε παρόμοιο μοτίβο, με θερμοκρασίες υψηλότερες από τις συνηθισμένες για την εποχή.

in.title: China's climate practices take center stage at COP31: cross-sector collaboration between meteorology and energy offers a Chinese approach to global climate adaptation
in.description: ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A thematic side event titled "From Early Warning to Energy Action: Pathways for Global Climate Diplomacy and Cooperation" was successfully held in the Blue Zone in Antalya, Türkiye, on November 13, during the 31st UN Climate Change Conference. COP31 The event was jointly hosted by the United Nations Institute for Training and Research and the Public Meteorological Service Centre of the China Meteorological Administration (National Early Warning Information Release Center), with strategic support from China Energy News, the foreign affairs working committee of the China Energy Research Society, and the China Institute of Energy Economics Research. Against the backdrop of increasingly severe global climate risks, the Climate Leadership Impact (CLI) initiative, jointly established by China Energy News, the China Energy Research Society and a number of other institutions and enterprises, was also officially launched. As a cross-sector collaboration platform, CLI aims to promote deeper integration between the meteorological and energy sectors across four key areas: risk governance and financial support, AI-powered forecasting and decision-making tools, coordinated clean energy dispatch, and interdisciplinary talent development. China Energy and Automobile Media Group During the event, CLI also presented the latest findings of its report, From Early Warning to Energy Action: 2026 Innovation Showcase on China's Corporate Actions and Collaborative Practices. Amid intensifying global climate change and growing risks from extreme weather, coordinating the low-carbon transition with climate adaptation and ensuring the security of energy systems have become major challenges facing the international community. Guided by its goals of peaking carbon emissions and achieving carbon neutrality, China is advancing its new energy security strategy of "four revolutions and one cooperation" and accelerating the development of a new energy system. As climate risks increasingly affect energy infrastructure and the balance between supply and demand, integrating meteorological information throughout the entire energy industry chain has become a shared priority across the sector. It was against this backdrop that the initiative to share the findings of "From Climate Early Warnings to Energy Action" was launched under the framework of the CLI. The working team began soliciting case studies in mid-June 2026. Over approximately four and a half months, the report underwent multiple rounds of refinement, including outline development, case selection, initial drafting, expert reviews, verification by participating enterprises and simultaneous revisions in Chinese and English. During the process, experts from various fields, including the China Electricity Council, China Huaneng Group and meteorological authorities, provided rigorous reviews to ensure the report's scientific rigor, practical value for the industry and effectiveness in international communication. China's Experience Dr Wang Jingyu, assistant director of the national key laboratory of advanced electromagnetic technology at Huazhong University of Science and Technology and an associate research fellow, who led the main report-writing team, presented its findings at the event. Dr Wang Jingyu, assistant director of the national key laboratory of advanced electromagnetic technology at Huazhong University of Science and Technology and an associate research fellow gave a speech The report systematically reviews innovative practices by Chinese enterprises and research institutions and summarizes the technical pathways and supporting mechanisms for translating early warnings into concrete action. It highlights three key insights: First, coordinated progress. The low-carbon transition in the energy sector and climate adaptation should advance in tandem, allowing emissions reduction achievements and energy system security to reinforce each other. Second, targeted application. The key is to integrate meteorological and climate information with equipment conditions, network structures and energy consumption needs, so as to identify priority areas for protection and determine the appropriate timing for action. Third, comprehensive support. Policy support and services, market-based financing, corporate governance and talent collaboration provide a strong foundation for the sustained implementation of technological advances. In terms of practical applications, the report covers four major areas: energy transition and climate risks, the operational application of forecasting and early warning systems, policy and service support, and China's practical experience. It features 16 case studies across six categories, including renewable energy output forecasting, energy infrastructure protection, power grid risk assessment, and dispatch and maintenance, ensuring energy supplies for key users and power restoration, flexible adjustment of energy supply and demand, and emissions reduction and carbon sequestration. These cases not only demonstrate measurable achievements in improving renewable energy integration, ensuring energy supply security, reducing disaster-related losses and enhancing operational efficiency, but also show how some of China's technologies and models have already been applied overseas. They offer valuable Chinese experience for the global energy sector in addressing climate change and advancing the development of new energy systems.

sg.title: Beyond AI Adoption: Hong Kong's Next Challenge Is Making AI Work Smarter
sg.description: As AI adoption becomes mainstream, LongbridgeAI explores how reducing repetitive tasks and making information more accessible can help bridge Hong Kong's productivity gap. HONG KONG and SINGAPORE, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Artificial intelligence (AI) has become an increasingly familiar part of everyday work in Hong Kong. Yet despite widespread adoption, translating its capabilities into meaningful improvements in how people work remains a challenge. According to a 2026 McKinsey study, 70% of Hong Kong's white-collar workers have adopted AI tools, with 88% of users reporting productivity improvements. However, fewer than a quarter use AI to execute complete workflows from beginning to end. The findings highlight a gap between AI adoption and deeper integration into everyday activities. While AI has made it easier to access information and complete individual tasks, many users continue to incorporate it into existing routines rather than fundamentally changing how work is organised. The next challenge for Hong Kong is therefore not simply getting more people to use AI, but making it work more effectively for those already using it. The Hidden Cost of Repetitive Information Gathering Consider how much time people spend keeping themselves informed. Whether following industry developments, checking the latest news or preparing regular reports, many activities involve gathering similar information from multiple sources. AI has made these tasks easier, but the experience often remains reactive. Users ask a question, receive a response and repeat the process whenever they need an update. Microsoft's 2026 Work Trend Index reinforces this challenge. In Hong Kong, 57% of surveyed AI users said it felt safer to focus on existing goals rather than redesign how they work with AI. The opportunity lies in moving beyond answering individual questions towards reducing the repetitive steps involved in accessing information. From Reactive AI to More Proactive Assistance LongbridgeAI’s Scheduled Tasks save time by delivering recurring updates automatically One emerging approach is using AI to automate recurring information requests. Rather than manually asking the same questions every day, users can define what information they need and when they want it delivered. For instance, someone following developments across multiple industries could schedule a daily summary of relevant news. Similarly, regular information updates could be organised around weekly or monthly routines. This reflects a broader shift in conversational AI: moving beyond individual questions towards supporting more structured, user-defined workflows. The broader evolution of task-oriented AI is also gaining attention in Hong Kong. At Hong Kong FinTech Week 2026, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced Project SAGE, an initiative supporting the responsible development of agentic AI in financial services, with a focus on practical applications, interoperability and governance. While agentic AI encompasses capabilities beyond scheduled automation, both developments reflect growing interest in AI systems that can perform defined tasks rather than simply respond to individual prompts. Why Smarter AI Still Needs Human Judgement Greater automation does not necessarily translate into better information or decisions. An AI-generated summary may be delivered automatically, but its contents could still be inaccurate, incomplete or outdated. McKinsey's Hong Kong findings illustrate this distinction. While more than 90% of surveyed AI users were comfortable using AI for supporting tasks, only 40% expressed comfort with full workflow automation. The contrast highlights an important principle: automating information gathering should not mean delegating judgement. As AI becomes more integrated into everyday routines, users must retain control over how tasks are defined, how outputs are reviewed and how information is ultimately used. Turning AI's Potential into Everyday Utility As the conversation around AI shifts from adoption to practical application, the focus is increasingly on making technology more useful in everyday routines. This is an area that LongbridgeAI, an AI-powered conversational platform, is exploring through its Scheduled Tasks feature, introduced in October 2026. Instead of repeatedly entering the same requests, users can configure AI tasks to run at daily, weekly or monthly intervals. Whether preparing a recurring information briefing, following developments on a topic of interest or organising regular summaries, the feature enables users to establish their information needs in advance and receive AI-generated results through the platform's Message Center. The significance lies not simply in automating individual requests, but in making AI more adaptable to how people access and manage information. Importantly, automation does not replace the need for human oversight. Users remain responsible for reviewing AI-generated content, verifying its accuracy and determining how the information should be used. For Hong Kong, where AI adoption is already widespread, the opportunity lies in making these technologies more relevant to everyday routines while maintaining appropriate safeguards. Ultimately, the next chapter of AI will not be defined simply by how many people use it, but by how effectively it helps people access information, reduce repetitive work and remain in control. Combining deep financial market expertise with cutting-edge AI capabilities, Longbridge AI develops intelligent solutions that transform how individuals and institutions access information, analyse markets, and make informed decisions. Through its AI-powered tools and strategic industry collaborations, Longbridge AI aims to make institutional-grade intelligence more actionable, intuitive, and accessible. With a vision to pioneer the next era of AI-native solutions, Longbridge AI is committed to building a holistic ecosystem where technology empowers human judgement.

sg.title: côte&ciel × Joe Chia capsule collection "What We Carry"
sg.description: Summary côte&ciel and Joe Chia launch the "What We Carry" capsule collection. Origami-folded cotton LINGGI convertible backpack and fluid ENDAU crossbody bag. Available globally today with prices ranging from $310 - $370 USD. côte&ciel has teamed up with Malaysian minimalist designer Joe Chia on “What We Carry,” a two-piece bag capsule about how material and movement interact. Known for translating architectural geometry into ergonomic bags, côte&ciel meets Chia’s fluid, garment-focused tailoring in a project exploring both physical materiality and emotional weight. As Joe Goodwin from côte&ciel's marketing team notes, the duo aimed to unpack "what we carry" - not just literally, but emotionally - acknowledging how past experiences shape the way individuals move through the world. By filtering the brand's sculptural archives through Chia’s apparel sensibilities, the partnership creates what Goodwin describes as a sense of "jamais vu": an aesthetic that feels simultaneously familiar and entirely unexpected. Both bags are named after rivers in Malaysia, a nod to Joe Chia’s roots and the idea of flow. The LINGGI is a convertible backpack that also wears as a shoulder bag. Its crossed straps meet a soft, teardrop-shaped body that sags and fills out depending on its contents. As for the ENDAU, it's a crossbody that can also go over one shoulder. A single strap tapers into a sculpted, drop-like body, and in the product shots it hangs almost like draped fabric. Both bags are made from black cotton with a crinkled, textured surface. They’re built with an origami-style folded construction and have expandable main compartments that fit laptops up to 16 inches, though neither has a dedicated laptop sleeve. Small details tie the collaboration together. Satin-finish metal teardrop zip pulls carry embossed côte&ciel branding, and a black strap slider bears both brands’ names. Inside, a lined interior includes a zippered pocket for smaller items. The all-black, texture-led palette keeps the attention on shape and drape. The côte&ciel x Joe Chia “What We Carry” capsule launches globally today via coteetciel.com, with prices from $310 - $370 USD. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Tersedia secara global hari ini dengan harga berkisar antara $310 - $370 USD. côte&ciel berkolaborasi dengan desainer minimalis asal Malaysia, Joe Chia, melansir "What We Carry," sebuah koleksi kapsul dua tas yang mengeksplorasi interaksi antara material dan pergerakan. Dikenal akan kepiawaiannya menerjemahkan struktur geometri arsitektural ke dalam desain tas ergonomis, gaya khas côte&ciel berpadu apik dengan teknik tailoring Chia yang fluid dan berfokus pada garmen. Proyek ini mendalami makna materialitas secara fisik sekaligus beban emosional. Seperti yang diungkapkan oleh Joe Goodwin dari tim pemasaran côte&ciel, kolaborasi ini bertujuan untuk mengurai makna "what we carry" — tidak hanya secara harfiah, tetapi juga secara emosional — yang merepresentasikan bagaimana rentetan pengalaman masa lalu membentuk cara seseorang melangkah di dunia. Dengan meleburkan arsip desain skulptural côte&ciel bersama kepekaan pakaian khas Chia, kemitraan ini menciptakan sesuatu yang Goodwin deskripsikan sebagai sensasi "jamais vu": sebuah estetika yang terasa familier namun pada saat yang sama, sungguh tak terduga. Kedua tas ini dinamakan dari sungai-sungai di Malaysia, sebagai bentuk penghormatan terhadap akar budaya Joe Chia dan konsep aliran yang dinamis. LINGGI adalah backpack serbaguna yang juga dapat dikenakan sebagai shoulder bag. Tali berpotongan silangnya menyatu dengan kompartemen utama berdesain menyerupai tetesan air yang lembut, di mana siluetnya dapat meluruh atau tampak berisi tergantung pada barang bawaan di dalamnya. Sementara itu, ENDAU adalah tas crossbody yang juga fleksibel disampirkan di satu bahu. Tali tunggalnya mengerucut menjadi bodi skulptural menyerupai tetesan air, dan dalam foto kampanyenya, tas ini tampak menggantung indah layaknya draperi kain. Kedua tas ini terbuat dari material katun hitam dengan efek permukaan kusut yang bertekstur. Desainnya mengusung konstruksi lipatan bergaya origami serta kompartemen utama yang dapat dilebarkan untuk memuat laptop berukuran hingga 16 inci, meskipun tidak dilengkapi saku laptop khusus. Detail-detail kecil turut menyempurnakan kolaborasi ini. Tarikan ritsleting metal berdesain tetesan air dengan satin-finish dihiasi ukiran logo côte&ciel, sementara slider tali berwarna hitam menampilkan nama kedua label. Di bagian dalam, interior berlapisnya dilengkapi saku ritsleting untuk menyimpan barang-barang berukuran kecil. Palet serba hitam yang menonjolkan permainan tekstur memastikan fokus tetap tertuju pada bentuk dan efek draperi tas. ph.title: China's climate practices take center stage at COP31: cross-sector collaboration between meteorology and energy offers a Chinese approach to global climate adaptation
ph.description: ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A thematic side event titled "From Early Warning to Energy Action: Pathways for Global Climate Diplomacy and Cooperation" was successfully held in the Blue Zone in Antalya, Türkiye, on November 13, during the 31st UN Climate Change Conference. COP31 The event was jointly hosted by the United Nations Institute for Training and Research and the Public Meteorological Service Centre of the China Meteorological Administration (National Early Warning Information Release Center), with strategic support from China Energy News, the foreign affairs working committee of the China Energy Research Society, and the China Institute of Energy Economics Research. Against the backdrop of increasingly severe global climate risks, the Climate Leadership Impact (CLI) initiative, jointly established by China Energy News, the China Energy Research Society and a number of other institutions and enterprises, was also officially launched. As a cross-sector collaboration platform, CLI aims to promote deeper integration between the meteorological and energy sectors across four key areas: risk governance and financial support, AI-powered forecasting and decision-making tools, coordinated clean energy dispatch, and interdisciplinary talent development. China Energy and Automobile Media Group During the event, CLI also presented the latest findings of its report, From Early Warning to Energy Action: 2026 Innovation Showcase on China's Corporate Actions and Collaborative Practices. Amid intensifying global climate change and growing risks from extreme weather, coordinating the low-carbon transition with climate adaptation and ensuring the security of energy systems have become major challenges facing the international community. Guided by its goals of peaking carbon emissions and achieving carbon neutrality, China is advancing its new energy security strategy of "four revolutions and one cooperation" and accelerating the development of a new energy system. As climate risks increasingly affect energy infrastructure and the balance between supply and demand, integrating meteorological information throughout the entire energy industry chain has become a shared priority across the sector. It was against this backdrop that the initiative to share the findings of "From Climate Early Warnings to Energy Action" was launched under the framework of the CLI. The working team began soliciting case studies in mid-June 2026. Over approximately four and a half months, the report underwent multiple rounds of refinement, including outline development, case selection, initial drafting, expert reviews, verification by participating enterprises and simultaneous revisions in Chinese and English. During the process, experts from various fields, including the China Electricity Council, China Huaneng Group and meteorological authorities, provided rigorous reviews to ensure the report's scientific rigor, practical value for the industry and effectiveness in international communication. China's Experience Dr Wang Jingyu, assistant director of the national key laboratory of advanced electromagnetic technology at Huazhong University of Science and Technology and an associate research fellow, who led the main report-writing team, presented its findings at the event. Dr Wang Jingyu, assistant director of the national key laboratory of advanced electromagnetic technology at Huazhong University of Science and Technology and an associate research fellow gave a speech The report systematically reviews innovative practices by Chinese enterprises and research institutions and summarizes the technical pathways and supporting mechanisms for translating early warnings into concrete action. It highlights three key insights: First, coordinated progress. The low-carbon transition in the energy sector and climate adaptation should advance in tandem, allowing emissions reduction achievements and energy system security to reinforce each other. Second, targeted application. The key is to integrate meteorological and climate information with equipment conditions, network structures and energy consumption needs, so as to identify priority areas for protection and determine the appropriate timing for action. Third, comprehensive support. Policy support and services, market-based financing, corporate governance and talent collaboration provide a strong foundation for the sustained implementation of technological advances. In terms of practical applications, the report covers four major areas: energy transition and climate risks, the operational application of forecasting and early warning systems, policy and service support, and China's practical experience. It features 16 case studies across six categories, including renewable energy output forecasting, energy infrastructure protection, power grid risk assessment, and dispatch and maintenance, ensuring energy supplies for key users and power restoration, flexible adjustment of energy supply and demand, and emissions reduction and carbon sequestration. These cases not only demonstrate measurable achievements in improving renewable energy integration, ensuring energy supply security, reducing disaster-related losses and enhancing operational efficiency, but also show how some of China's technologies and models have already been applied overseas. They offer valuable Chinese experience for the global energy sector in addressing climate change and advancing the development of new energy systems.

ph.title: Beyond AI Adoption: Hong Kong's Next Challenge Is Making AI Work Smarter
ph.description: As AI adoption becomes mainstream, LongbridgeAI explores how reducing repetitive tasks and making information more accessible can help bridge Hong Kong's productivity gap. HONG KONG and SINGAPORE, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Artificial intelligence (AI) has become an increasingly familiar part of everyday work in Hong Kong. Yet despite widespread adoption, translating its capabilities into meaningful improvements in how people work remains a challenge. According to a 2026 McKinsey study, 70% of Hong Kong's white-collar workers have adopted AI tools, with 88% of users reporting productivity improvements. However, fewer than a quarter use AI to execute complete workflows from beginning to end. The findings highlight a gap between AI adoption and deeper integration into everyday activities. While AI has made it easier to access information and complete individual tasks, many users continue to incorporate it into existing routines rather than fundamentally changing how work is organised. The next challenge for Hong Kong is therefore not simply getting more people to use AI, but making it work more effectively for those already using it. The Hidden Cost of Repetitive Information Gathering Consider how much time people spend keeping themselves informed. Whether following industry developments, checking the latest news or preparing regular reports, many activities involve gathering similar information from multiple sources. AI has made these tasks easier, but the experience often remains reactive. Users ask a question, receive a response and repeat the process whenever they need an update. Microsoft's 2026 Work Trend Index reinforces this challenge. In Hong Kong, 57% of surveyed AI users said it felt safer to focus on existing goals rather than redesign how they work with AI. The opportunity lies in moving beyond answering individual questions towards reducing the repetitive steps involved in accessing information. From Reactive AI to More Proactive Assistance LongbridgeAI’s Scheduled Tasks save time by delivering recurring updates automatically One emerging approach is using AI to automate recurring information requests. Rather than manually asking the same questions every day, users can define what information they need and when they want it delivered. For instance, someone following developments across multiple industries could schedule a daily summary of relevant news. Similarly, regular information updates could be organised around weekly or monthly routines. This reflects a broader shift in conversational AI: moving beyond individual questions towards supporting more structured, user-defined workflows. The broader evolution of task-oriented AI is also gaining attention in Hong Kong. At Hong Kong FinTech Week 2026, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced Project SAGE, an initiative supporting the responsible development of agentic AI in financial services, with a focus on practical applications, interoperability and governance. While agentic AI encompasses capabilities beyond scheduled automation, both developments reflect growing interest in AI systems that can perform defined tasks rather than simply respond to individual prompts. Why Smarter AI Still Needs Human Judgement Greater automation does not necessarily translate into better information or decisions. An AI-generated summary may be delivered automatically, but its contents could still be inaccurate, incomplete or outdated. McKinsey's Hong Kong findings illustrate this distinction. While more than 90% of surveyed AI users were comfortable using AI for supporting tasks, only 40% expressed comfort with full workflow automation. The contrast highlights an important principle: automating information gathering should not mean delegating judgement. As AI becomes more integrated into everyday routines, users must retain control over how tasks are defined, how outputs are reviewed and how information is ultimately used. Turning AI's Potential into Everyday Utility As the conversation around AI shifts from adoption to practical application, the focus is increasingly on making technology more useful in everyday routines. This is an area that LongbridgeAI, an AI-powered conversational platform, is exploring through its Scheduled Tasks feature, introduced in October 2026. Instead of repeatedly entering the same requests, users can configure AI tasks to run at daily, weekly or monthly intervals. Whether preparing a recurring information briefing, following developments on a topic of interest or organising regular summaries, the feature enables users to establish their information needs in advance and receive AI-generated results through the platform's Message Center. The significance lies not simply in automating individual requests, but in making AI more adaptable to how people access and manage information. Importantly, automation does not replace the need for human oversight. Users remain responsible for reviewing AI-generated content, verifying its accuracy and determining how the information should be used. For Hong Kong, where AI adoption is already widespread, the opportunity lies in making these technologies more relevant to everyday routines while maintaining appropriate safeguards. Ultimately, the next chapter of AI will not be defined simply by how many people use it, but by how effectively it helps people access information, reduce repetitive work and remain in control. About LongbridgeAI Longbridge AI Technologies Limited ("Longbridge AI") is the artificial intelligence arm of AI-native financial technology company, Longbridge Group, dedicated to advancing the development and responsible adoption of AI technology. Combining deep financial market expertise with cutting-edge AI capabilities, Longbridge AI develops intelligent solutions that transform how individuals and institutions access information, analyse markets, and make informed decisions. Through its AI-powered tools and strategic industry collaborations, Longbridge AI aims to make institutional-grade intelligence more actionable, intuitive, and accessible. With a vision to pioneer the next era of AI-native solutions, Longbridge AI is committed to building a holistic ecosystem where technology empowers human judgement.

ph.title: Cebu sustains P237-M agricultural damage in 2 months from El Niño
ph.description: CEBU CITY – The province of Cebu on Friday reported P237 million in agricultural damage from El Niño. In a damage assessment report from October to November, the Provincial Agriculture Office (PAO) reported that agricultural damage in Cebu reached P237.2 million, with the corn sector the most severely affected at P182.5 million. Provincial Agriculturist Roldan Saragena said P54.6 million in high-value cops were lost and 1,468 hectares of agricultural land in eight municipalities have been affected. Saragena said the extent of damage may further increase as the drought is expected to last for several more months. In a southern town in the province, private refilling stations will play a key to help cushion the impact of the drought. The local government of Minglanilla has tapped water refilling stations to establish alternative water sources in barangays. Acting Mayor Lheslen Enad said the town has signed a Memorandum of Agreement with 23 water refilling station operators in an initiative that will make their establishments community water points for residents affected by limited water supply. The partnership aims to collect and store wastewater generated during the water filtration process that will allow residents to reuse it for household activities that do not require potable water. Water refilling stations produce only about 40 percent potable water through reverse osmosis, while the remaining 60 percent is discharged as wastewater, Enad said. Under the agreement, wastewater collected will be used for washing, laundry, and bathing. "We will store it and share it with the community where the station is located," Enad said. The local government will provide participating establishments with tanks that can store 1,000 to 2,000 liters of water. These facilities will be used as accessible water points for residents, particularly those living in areas where water supply becomes scarce during prolonged dry spells.

bd.title: China's climate practices take center stage at COP31: cross-sector collaboration between meteorology and energy offers a Chinese approach to global climate adaptation
bd.description: ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A thematic side event titled "From Early Warning to Energy Action: Pathways for Global Climate Diplomacy and Cooperation" was successfully held in the Blue Zone in Antalya, Türkiye, on November 13, during the 31st UN Climate Change Conference. COP31 The event was jointly hosted by the United Nations Institute for Training and Research and the Public Meteorological Service Centre of the China Meteorological Administration (National Early Warning Information Release Center), with strategic support from China Energy News, the foreign affairs working committee of the China Energy Research Society, and the China Institute of Energy Economics Research. Against the backdrop of increasingly severe global climate risks, the Climate Leadership Impact (CLI) initiative, jointly established by China Energy News, the China Energy Research Society and a number of other institutions and enterprises, was also officially launched. As a cross-sector collaboration platform, CLI aims to promote deeper integration between the meteorological and energy sectors across four key areas: risk governance and financial support, AI-powered forecasting and decision-making tools, coordinated clean energy dispatch, and interdisciplinary talent development. China Energy and Automobile Media Group During the event, CLI also presented the latest findings of its report, From Early Warning to Energy Action: 2026 Innovation Showcase on China's Corporate Actions and Collaborative Practices. Amid intensifying global climate change and growing risks from extreme weather, coordinating the low-carbon transition with climate adaptation and ensuring the security of energy systems have become major challenges facing the international community. Guided by its goals of peaking carbon emissions and achieving carbon neutrality, China is advancing its new energy security strategy of "four revolutions and one cooperation" and accelerating the development of a new energy system. As climate risks increasingly affect energy infrastructure and the balance between supply and demand, integrating meteorological information throughout the entire energy industry chain has become a shared priority across the sector. It was against this backdrop that the initiative to share the findings of "From Climate Early Warnings to Energy Action" was launched under the framework of the CLI. The working team began soliciting case studies in mid-June 2026. Over approximately four and a half months, the report underwent multiple rounds of refinement, including outline development, case selection, initial drafting, expert reviews, verification by participating enterprises and simultaneous revisions in Chinese and English. During the process, experts from various fields, including the China Electricity Council, China Huaneng Group and meteorological authorities, provided rigorous reviews to ensure the report's scientific rigor, practical value for the industry and effectiveness in international communication. China's Experience Dr Wang Jingyu, assistant director of the national key laboratory of advanced electromagnetic technology at Huazhong University of Science and Technology and an associate research fellow, who led the main report-writing team, presented its findings at the event. Dr Wang Jingyu, assistant director of the national key laboratory of advanced electromagnetic technology at Huazhong University of Science and Technology and an associate research fellow gave a speech The report systematically reviews innovative practices by Chinese enterprises and research institutions and summarizes the technical pathways and supporting mechanisms for translating early warnings into concrete action. It highlights three key insights: First, coordinated progress. The low-carbon transition in the energy sector and climate adaptation should advance in tandem, allowing emissions reduction achievements and energy system security to reinforce each other. Second, targeted application. The key is to integrate meteorological and climate information with equipment conditions, network structures and energy consumption needs, so as to identify priority areas for protection and determine the appropriate timing for action. Third, comprehensive support. Policy support and services, market-based financing, corporate governance and talent collaboration provide a strong foundation for the sustained implementation of technological advances. In terms of practical applications, the report covers four major areas: energy transition and climate risks, the operational application of forecasting and early warning systems, policy and service support, and China's practical experience. It features 16 case studies across six categories, including renewable energy output forecasting, energy infrastructure protection, power grid risk assessment, and dispatch and maintenance, ensuring energy supplies for key users and power restoration, flexible adjustment of energy supply and demand, and emissions reduction and carbon sequestration. These cases not only demonstrate measurable achievements in improving renewable energy integration, ensuring energy supply security, reducing disaster-related losses and enhancing operational efficiency, but also show how some of China's technologies and models have already been applied overseas. They offer valuable Chinese experience for the global energy sector in addressing climate change and advancing the development of new energy systems.

bd.title: Beyond AI Adoption: Hong Kong's Next Challenge Is Making AI Work Smarter
bd.description: As AI adoption becomes mainstream, LongbridgeAI explores how reducing repetitive tasks and making information more accessible can help bridge Hong Kong's productivity gap. HONG KONG and SINGAPORE, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Artificial intelligence (AI) has become an increasingly familiar part of everyday work in Hong Kong. Yet despite widespread adoption, translating its capabilities into meaningful improvements in how people work remains a challenge. According to a 2026 McKinsey study, 70% of Hong Kong's white-collar workers have adopted AI tools, with 88% of users reporting productivity improvements. However, fewer than a quarter use AI to execute complete workflows from beginning to end. The findings highlight a gap between AI adoption and deeper integration into everyday activities. While AI has made it easier to access information and complete individual tasks, many users continue to incorporate it into existing routines rather than fundamentally changing how work is organised. The next challenge for Hong Kong is therefore not simply getting more people to use AI, but making it work more effectively for those already using it. The Hidden Cost of Repetitive Information Gathering Consider how much time people spend keeping themselves informed. Whether following industry developments, checking the latest news or preparing regular reports, many activities involve gathering similar information from multiple sources. AI has made these tasks easier, but the experience often remains reactive. Users ask a question, receive a response and repeat the process whenever they need an update. Microsoft's 2026 Work Trend Index reinforces this challenge. In Hong Kong, 57% of surveyed AI users said it felt safer to focus on existing goals rather than redesign how they work with AI. The opportunity lies in moving beyond answering individual questions towards reducing the repetitive steps involved in accessing information. From Reactive AI to More Proactive Assistance LongbridgeAI’s Scheduled Tasks save time by delivering recurring updates automatically One emerging approach is using AI to automate recurring information requests. Rather than manually asking the same questions every day, users can define what information they need and when they want it delivered. For instance, someone following developments across multiple industries could schedule a daily summary of relevant news. Similarly, regular information updates could be organised around weekly or monthly routines. This reflects a broader shift in conversational AI: moving beyond individual questions towards supporting more structured, user-defined workflows. The broader evolution of task-oriented AI is also gaining attention in Hong Kong. At Hong Kong FinTech Week 2026, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced Project SAGE, an initiative supporting the responsible development of agentic AI in financial services, with a focus on practical applications, interoperability and governance. While agentic AI encompasses capabilities beyond scheduled automation, both developments reflect growing interest in AI systems that can perform defined tasks rather than simply respond to individual prompts. Why Smarter AI Still Needs Human Judgement Greater automation does not necessarily translate into better information or decisions. An AI-generated summary may be delivered automatically, but its contents could still be inaccurate, incomplete or outdated. McKinsey's Hong Kong findings illustrate this distinction. While more than 90% of surveyed AI users were comfortable using AI for supporting tasks, only 40% expressed comfort with full workflow automation. The contrast highlights an important principle: automating information gathering should not mean delegating judgement. As AI becomes more integrated into everyday routines, users must retain control over how tasks are defined, how outputs are reviewed and how information is ultimately used. Turning AI's Potential into Everyday Utility As the conversation around AI shifts from adoption to practical application, the focus is increasingly on making technology more useful in everyday routines. This is an area that LongbridgeAI, an AI-powered conversational platform, is exploring through its Scheduled Tasks feature, introduced in October 2026. Instead of repeatedly entering the same requests, users can configure AI tasks to run at daily, weekly or monthly intervals. Whether preparing a recurring information briefing, following developments on a topic of interest or organising regular summaries, the feature enables users to establish their information needs in advance and receive AI-generated results through the platform's Message Center. The significance lies not simply in automating individual requests, but in making AI more adaptable to how people access and manage information. Importantly, automation does not replace the need for human oversight. Users remain responsible for reviewing AI-generated content, verifying its accuracy and determining how the information should be used. For Hong Kong, where AI adoption is already widespread, the opportunity lies in making these technologies more relevant to everyday routines while maintaining appropriate safeguards. Ultimately, the next chapter of AI will not be defined simply by how many people use it, but by how effectively it helps people access information, reduce repetitive work and remain in control. Combining deep financial market expertise with cutting-edge AI capabilities, Longbridge AI develops intelligent solutions that transform how individuals and institutions access information, analyse markets, and make informed decisions. Through its AI-powered tools and strategic industry collaborations, Longbridge AI aims to make institutional-grade intelligence more actionable, intuitive, and accessible. With a vision to pioneer the next era of AI-native solutions, Longbridge AI is committed to building a holistic ecosystem where technology empowers human judgement.

bd.title: Embracing COP31 as a 'COP of Implementation': Side event explores pathways for global climate diplomacy and cooperation
bd.description: ANKARA, Turkey, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A thematic side event titled "From Early Warning to Energy Action: Pathways for Global Climate Diplomacy and Cooperation" was held on the afternoon of November 13 local time at the Global Alliance of Universities on Climate during the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change. The 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change. The event was jointly hosted by the United Nations Institute for Training and Research and the Public Meteorological Service Centre of the China Meteorological Administration (National Early Warning Information Release Center), with strategic support from China Energy News, the foreign affairs working committee of the China Energy Research Society (CERS), and the China Institute of Energy Economics Research. Representatives from Russia, China and various international organizations, including the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), attended the event. Participants held in-depth discussions on climate risk prevention, early warning systems, energy transition and international cooperation, exploring ways to effectively translate climate warnings into concrete energy actions. At the event, the Climate Leadership Impact (CLI) platform presented its first bilingual report in Chinese and English, titled "From Early Warning to Energy Action: 2026 Innovation Showcase on China's Corporate Actions and Collaborative Practices." The report highlights how measurable and replicable industrial practices can contribute to COP31's theme of a "COP of Implementation." Focusing on preventing climate disasters and enhancing climate resilience, it explores energy-led approaches to climate action, with the aim of bringing greater certainty and positive momentum to global climate governance. Joint efforts to translate early warnings into energy action The World Meteorological Organization's (WMO) State of the Global Climate Update 2026, released during the conference, shows that the global average surface temperature in the first nine months of 2026 was approximately 1.47 degrees above pre-industrial levels. An exceptionally strong El Niño event is expected to further intensify high temperatures and extreme weather, with impacts likely to continue into 2027. The number of countries with multi-hazard early warning systems has increased from 56 in 2015 to 136 in 2025. Meanwhile, the UN Environment Programme's Adaptation Gap Report 2026 estimates that developing countries will need approximately $305 billion annually in adaptation financing by 2035. Even if the target of tripling international public adaptation finance is achieved, it would cover only around 20 to 30 percent of the estimated needs. While early warning coverage is expanding, funding, institutional mechanisms and capacity have not kept pace. Sergey Kononuchenko, special representative of the Russian Foreign Ministry for climate issues and ambassador-at-large, said in his address that climate change is an urgent challenge facing humanity and that the priority now is to translate commitments into concrete action. He stressed the need to strengthen early warning systems through technological innovation, including artificial intelligence and satellite observation, to protect critical energy infrastructure; uphold multilateralism and ensure developing countries have equitable access to early warning technologies and capacity-building opportunities; and urge all parties, particularly developed countries, to honor their commitments on climate financing and technology transfer. He also recognized China's achievements in building the world's largest renewable energy system and carbon emissions trading market, expressing hope that COP31 would serve as a platform for practical action. "Early warning is not the end point, but the starting point for action," said Sun Zhengyun, vice chairman and secretary-general of the CERS. He noted that improvements in forecasting capabilities do not necessarily translate into stronger response capacities. To bridge this gap, Sun said, efforts should first be made to effectively connect climate early warnings with power grid dispatch, renewable energy generation forecasting, energy storage management and emergency response, ensuring that warning information is genuinely incorporated into energy system operations. Climate risk management should also be strengthened in energy planning and investment decisions to improve the resilience of projects from the outset. In addition, international cooperation should be deepened, with greater emphasis on capacity building in developing countries, enabling more regions to develop comprehensive capabilities to translate early warnings into action. Xie Rongbin, Party secretary, chairman and editor-in-chief of China Energy and Automobile Media Group Co Ltd, president of China Automotive News, and editor-in-chief of China Energy News, said the global energy transition is a systemic transformation requiring the coordinated management of climate risk early warnings, technological innovation, industrial collaboration, market mechanisms, security safeguards and equitable development. The key, Xie said, is to turn early warning capabilities into effective emergency responses. China is actively exploring ways to integrate meteorological warnings with energy dispatch, while using technology to strengthen the resilience of energy systems against extreme weather shocks. In July this year, China's installed solar power capacity surpassed that of coal-fired power, making solar the country's largest source of installed power capacity. Andrew Tupper, head of the Early Warning Services at the WMO, expressed agreement with this approach. He noted that conventional, general-purpose weather warnings are no longer sufficient to meet current needs. There is an urgent need to establish "impact-based early warning systems" that connect meteorological information with energy operations, enabling warnings to trigger timely and targeted protective measures for energy assets. Bridging meteorology and energy through cross-sector collaboration Sergey Kononuchenko, special representative of the Russian Foreign Ministry As a core member of the research team behind the report From Climate Early Warnings to Energy Action: 2026 Progress Report on Chinese Enterprises' Actions and Collaborative Practices, Dr. Wang Jingyu, assistant director of the national key laboratory of advanced electromagnetic technology at Huazhong University of Science and Technology and an associate research fellow, presented the CLI platform's first bilingual report in Chinese and English. Wang said the report features 16 practical case studies across six categories, covering renewable energy output forecasting, infrastructure protection, power grid dispatch and maintenance, energy security for key users, supply-demand adjustment, and emissions reduction and carbon sequestration. Ye Dong, a senior researcher at the Public Meteorological Service Centre of the China Meteorological Administration, introduced initiatives to harness AI for energy-related meteorological and climate services under the theme "From Accurate Forecasting to Enhanced Climate Resilience." Ye noted that meteorological conditions have a profound impact on the entire energy chain, from production and transmission to consumption. As global climate change intensifies, extreme weather poses increasingly prominent threats to energy systems. Meanwhile, non-disaster weather conditions with significant impacts, such as prolonged periods of weak winds and reduced sunshine, can also cause fluctuations in renewable energy output and disrupt the balance between electricity supply and demand. Specialized meteorological early warning services for the energy sector are therefore essential to ensuring energy security and strengthening the climate resilience of energy systems, Ye said. China is actively developing AI-based meteorological forecasting models tailored to energy-sector applications, drawing on domestically developed satellites and multi-source observation data. Ye stressed that AI is merely a technological tool, and that the key is to address real-world operational needs and translate accurate weather forecasts and warnings into concrete measures for protecting energy facilities, power dispatch and risk response. Practical applications on the power grid side have already established a complete chain from forecasting to response. State Grid Shaanxi Electric Power, drawing on standardized observation systems at power stations and the "Fuxi" meteorological foundation model, has achieved an accuracy rate of 95.2 percent in short-term power output forecasting. Its icing warnings now provide an additional 18 hours of lead time, while the initiative has cumulatively enabled an additional 65.05 million kilowatt-hours of renewable electricity generation. State Grid Zhoushan Power Supply Company in East China's Zhejiang Province has used a large AI model to coordinate preparations before disasters, emergency response during disasters and post-disaster repairs, reducing the average time needed to complete the fault-resolution process from eight hours to 4.7 hours. On the enterprise side, early warnings are being translated into economic returns and asset protection. China Resources Power Technology Institute has developed an integrated climate and energy storage management platform. Based on operational data from a wind power project equipped with energy storage in Central China's Hubei Province during the first half of this year, the platform is estimated to reduce renewable energy curtailment by 92.6 percent and increase overall economic benefits by more than 10 million yuan. Trina Solar has integrated module protection, grid-forming energy storage, and intelligent operation and maintenance. Estimates based on a 100-megawatt solar project in Texas, the US, indicate that the approach could reduce average annual asset losses by 94 percent, demonstrating the potential for similar solutions to be replicated in overseas regions facing high climate risks. Policy support is also creating an institutional framework for closer coordination between meteorology and the energy sector. In January this year, the China Meteorological Administration and the National Energy Administration jointly issued guidelines on developing an energy meteorological service system, setting out 20 tasks and aiming to establish an integrated energy meteorological service system covering all energy-sector scenarios by 2027. Tian Yuyang, assistant director of the foreign affairs working committee of the CERS, said the CLI platform would continue to advance its work across four areas: risk governance and financial support, AI-enabled forecasting and decision-making, coordinated clean energy dispatch, and interdisciplinary talent development. The goal is to translate research findings into operational applications and turn pilot experience into industry standards. China Energy and Automobile Media Group Co Ltd Under the theme "How can meteorological warnings be effectively translated into action within energy systems?" three representatives of international organizations – Tupper, Avishek Malla, head of renewable energy at the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), and Binu Parthan, deputy director of country engagement and partnerships at IRENA – joined enterprise representatives, including Wu Xiao, vice president of Trina Solar and head of the group's ESG management and risk control, and Han Shutong, general manager of LONGi Green Energy Technology's UK representative office, for an in-depth discussion. The session was moderated by He Chaoxin, chief youth officer of the Global Alliance of Universities on Climate. Tupper pointed out that the bottleneck in cross-sector collaboration lies not in information sharing itself, but in whether energy departments genuinely rely on meteorological warnings when making dispatch decisions. Without trust built through long-term cooperation, warnings may remain merely reference information rather than becoming a basis for decision-making. The WMO is now incorporating this model of trust-based collaboration into its global early warning framework, promoting a shift from basic cooperation between meteorological and energy departments toward substantive operational coordination, Tupper said. Malla presented practical achievements in mountainous areas of South Asia. ICIMOD has established a multi-tiered early warning system that includes high-resolution forecasts up to 54 hours ahead, flood forecasts 10 to 15 days in advance and glacial lake outburst monitoring. Information is shared with government departments and local communities, while text messages and alerts are used to deliver warnings directly to the public. The center is also incorporating climate data into sensitivity analysis models used by hydropower investors and commercial banks, opening up new channels for integrating climate information into risk assessments of energy infrastructure. Parthan focused on the implementation stage after warnings are issued. Taking heatwaves as an example, he noted that high temperatures both reduce the transmission capacity of power lines and drive up electricity demand for cooling. However, such warning information has not yet been effectively incorporated into the operational planning of utility companies. He proposed bringing together multiple stakeholders, including power grid planners, government departments, system operators and financial institutions, to establish cross-sector mechanisms for short-term decision-making. This would enable early warning information to directly inform real-time energy system dispatch and investment decisions. Participants agreed that the main bottleneck in translating early warnings into action is shifting from meteorological technology to the operational rules of energy systems. The CLI platform's first progress report is a response to this challenge. By turning the practical experience of Chinese enterprises in dispatch response, resilience upgrades and cross-border cooperation into measurable and replicable industry references, the report aims to help transform COP31's theme of a "COP of Implementation" from a conference slogan into concrete action within energy systems. During the conference, China's approaches also offered developing countries new options for addressing gaps in their climate response capabilities. On November 11, China's AI-powered meteorological early warning solution, the "Mazu" all-in-one system, was unveiled to a global audience at a high-level forum on South-South cooperation on climate change. As of October 2026, the system had been deployed in eight countries, including Pakistan, Ethiopia and Sri Lanka, and was undergoing cloud-based trials in more than 50 countries. On November 12, He Yang, deputy head of the National Energy Administration, said at a high-level event on the Global Grid Accelerator initiative that China was willing to support countries in building power grids that ensure energy security and prosperity through a model of "shared provision."

bd.title: TÜV SÜD opens its International Technology & Innovation Campus in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area
bd.description: Building a New Global Hub for New Energy Testing and Certification GUANGZHOU, China, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On 20 November 2026, TÜV SÜD has officially inaugurated its International Technology & Innovation Campus in the Greater Bay Area (GBA). The new campus will serve as a platform for energy technology innovation, testing, certification, and quality infrastructure services, connecting innovation in China with global markets. By combining advanced testing capabilities with TÜV SÜD's global technical expertise, the campus will help to build trust in emerging technologies and support their safe and successful deployment in international markets. It will serve as a strategic innovation hub within the Group's Asia-Pacific network. The launch marks an important milestone in TÜV SÜD's continued development in the GBA and reinforces the Group's role in supporting the safe, sustainable and trusted development of future industries worldwide. Those in attendance at the opening ceremony included Dr. Josefine Wallat, Consul General of the Federal Republic of Germany in Guangzhou; Ishan Palit, Member of the Board of Management and Chief Operating Officer of TÜV SÜD AG; Dirk von Wahl, Chief Executive Officer of TÜV SÜD North Asia; Andrew Lee, Chief Financial Officer of TÜV SÜD North Asia; and Boris Ouyang, General Manager of TÜV SÜD Guangzhou. Together with government representatives, industry partners, customers and members of the media, they witnessed the official opening of the TÜV SÜD International Technology & Innovation Campus. Group photo at the opening ceremony of the TÜV SÜD International Technology & Innovation Campus Building an International Technology & Innovation Platform in the GBA The campus is being developed in three phases. The first phase comprises approximately 15,000 square metres, once all three phases are complete, the campus will span over 50,000 square metres. It brings together TÜV SÜD's 160 years of technical expertise and global network with local research, development, testing and operational capabilities. This combination is designed to strengthen confidence in new energy technologies and connect innovation from the Greater Bay Area with global markets. The new campus will collaborate with TÜV SÜD's existing testing centre in Panyu, Guangzhou, to enhance technical capabilities, especially in future-oriented fields such as advanced energy storage, robotics, artificial intelligence data centres, and digital trust. This will further strengthen TÜV SÜD's capacity to support manufacturers in China and international markets via a connected network of specialised testing facilities and technical expertise. Speaking at the ceremony, Ishan Palit, Member of the Board of Management and Chief Operating Officer of TÜV SÜD AG, said: "This campus represents a strategic investment in the technologies that are shaping the future of energy and industry. It will strengthen TÜV SÜD's ability to support customers through the energy transition and changing global supply chains. Technology is transforming the way energy is generated, stored and used. Our role is to facilitate building trust in this transformation by providing technical excellence, independent testing and certification, and solutions that enable innovative technologies to reach markets safely and efficiently. Through this campus, we aim to go beyond testing and certification, helping customers to navigate technological change, build trust and unlock opportunities in global markets." A Global Perspective Supporting the International Growth of the New Energy Industry As the global drive towards carbon neutrality accelerates, international green trade rules, national energy-efficiency standards, and carbon-related trade barriers continue to evolve. This raises market access requirements across the global new energy sector. Product safety, system reliability, green and low-carbon performance, and international compliance capabilities have become essential foundations for companies competing in global markets. For new energy companies, demonstrating safety, performance and compliance across different markets is becoming an increasingly important prerequisite for international growth. In China, policy priorities are also accelerating the development of cleaner, more resilient energy systems, including new energy storage, smart grids and greater coordination between digital infrastructure and power systems. The International Technology & Innovation Campus is designed to connect China's rapid development of new technologies with international standards and market requirements. Addressing the challenges that new energy companies face when entering overseas markets, the campus draws on TÜV SÜD's global technical expertise and its international testing, certification and market access capabilities, to provide integrated support for international market access. This helps companies to shorten lead times, reduce costs, and strengthen compliance as they expand abroad. By combining local technical capabilities with global expertise and knowledge of international standards, the campus will help manufacturers demonstrate technical performance and regulatory compliance across markets, creating value beyond compliance and supporting companies in bringing innovation to market. The TÜV SÜD International Technology & Innovation Campus Advancing the New Energy Industry through Forward-Looking Standards In terms of service capabilities, the campus will focus on key application scenarios across the new energy industry. It will provide companies in the Greater Bay Area with integrated technical services, including R&D testing, safety validation, testing and certification, and international market access. These services will help companies to shorten time to market, reduce compliance risks, and strengthen their international competitiveness. pk.title: Beyond AI Adoption: Hong Kong's Next Challenge Is Making AI Work Smarter
pk.description: As AI adoption becomes mainstream, LongbridgeAI explores how reducing repetitive tasks and making information more accessible can help bridge Hong Kong's productivity gap. HONG KONG and SINGAPORE, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Artificial intelligence (AI) has become an increasingly familiar part of everyday work in Hong Kong. Yet despite widespread adoption, translating its capabilities into meaningful improvements in how people work remains a challenge. According to a 2026 McKinsey study, 70% of Hong Kong's white-collar workers have adopted AI tools, with 88% of users reporting productivity improvements. However, fewer than a quarter use AI to execute complete workflows from beginning to end. The findings highlight a gap between AI adoption and deeper integration into everyday activities. While AI has made it easier to access information and complete individual tasks, many users continue to incorporate it into existing routines rather than fundamentally changing how work is organised. The next challenge for Hong Kong is therefore not simply getting more people to use AI, but making it work more effectively for those already using it. The Hidden Cost of Repetitive Information Gathering Consider how much time people spend keeping themselves informed. Whether following industry developments, checking the latest news or preparing regular reports, many activities involve gathering similar information from multiple sources. AI has made these tasks easier, but the experience often remains reactive. Users ask a question, receive a response and repeat the process whenever they need an update. Microsoft's 2026 Work Trend Index reinforces this challenge. In Hong Kong, 57% of surveyed AI users said it felt safer to focus on existing goals rather than redesign how they work with AI. The opportunity lies in moving beyond answering individual questions towards reducing the repetitive steps involved in accessing information. From Reactive AI to More Proactive Assistance LongbridgeAI’s Scheduled Tasks save time by delivering recurring updates automatically One emerging approach is using AI to automate recurring information requests. Rather than manually asking the same questions every day, users can define what information they need and when they want it delivered. For instance, someone following developments across multiple industries could schedule a daily summary of relevant news. Similarly, regular information updates could be organised around weekly or monthly routines. This reflects a broader shift in conversational AI: moving beyond individual questions towards supporting more structured, user-defined workflows. The broader evolution of task-oriented AI is also gaining attention in Hong Kong. At Hong Kong FinTech Week 2026, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced Project SAGE, an initiative supporting the responsible development of agentic AI in financial services, with a focus on practical applications, interoperability and governance. While agentic AI encompasses capabilities beyond scheduled automation, both developments reflect growing interest in AI systems that can perform defined tasks rather than simply respond to individual prompts. Why Smarter AI Still Needs Human Judgement Greater automation does not necessarily translate into better information or decisions. An AI-generated summary may be delivered automatically, but its contents could still be inaccurate, incomplete or outdated. McKinsey's Hong Kong findings illustrate this distinction. While more than 90% of surveyed AI users were comfortable using AI for supporting tasks, only 40% expressed comfort with full workflow automation. The contrast highlights an important principle: automating information gathering should not mean delegating judgement. As AI becomes more integrated into everyday routines, users must retain control over how tasks are defined, how outputs are reviewed and how information is ultimately used. Turning AI's Potential into Everyday Utility As the conversation around AI shifts from adoption to practical application, the focus is increasingly on making technology more useful in everyday routines. This is an area that LongbridgeAI, an AI-powered conversational platform, is exploring through its Scheduled Tasks feature, introduced in October 2026. Instead of repeatedly entering the same requests, users can configure AI tasks to run at daily, weekly or monthly intervals. Whether preparing a recurring information briefing, following developments on a topic of interest or organising regular summaries, the feature enables users to establish their information needs in advance and receive AI-generated results through the platform's Message Center. The significance lies not simply in automating individual requests, but in making AI more adaptable to how people access and manage information. Importantly, automation does not replace the need for human oversight. Users remain responsible for reviewing AI-generated content, verifying its accuracy and determining how the information should be used. For Hong Kong, where AI adoption is already widespread, the opportunity lies in making these technologies more relevant to everyday routines while maintaining appropriate safeguards. Ultimately, the next chapter of AI will not be defined simply by how many people use it, but by how effectively it helps people access information, reduce repetitive work and remain in control.
